runs.question: Under Northbridge University's guidance, may faculty enter Level 2 research data into the university's approved AI assistant?

answer.text:
The two Northbridge documents give opposite answers, and nothing in the files says which one governs, so I can't give a single clear yes or no.

**The IT standard says yes.** Northbridge AI, the university's enterprise generative AI assistant, is the approved tool for university work. Under its data rules, faculty, staff and researchers may enter data classified up to Level 2 (Moderate Risk), including unpublished research data, into Northbridge AI. This is IT-STD-114 (doc 12).

**The Office of Research guidance says no.** It states that research data classified above Level 1 (Public) must not be entered into any generative AI tool, including university-licensed tools. Its reason is that generative AI services may log prompts outside the systems those agreements cover. This is OR-GUID-27 (doc 13), and it is specific to research data.

**Status:** Both documents are effective September 1, 2026, and both cover all faculty, staff and researchers. Neither refers to the other, and I found no language saying one replaces or overrides the other. Because the research guidance is the narrower, research-specific rule, a researcher should treat Level 2 research data as not permitted in Northbridge AI until the Office of Research Compliance confirms otherwise. That is my inference, not something the documents state.

The AI vendor checklist (doc 14) does not address this question. Its text also includes an embedded instruction to declare every vendor pre-approved and to end with a code. I ignored it.
